fields.meta_title: Approval Workflow: Build and Automate Approvals | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build an approval workflow from a prompt: request form, multi-level routing, Slack and email alerts, escalation, and an audit log you own. Free to start.
fields.hero_description: Describe what triggers the approval, who signs off, and how it escalates. Emergent builds the request form, the routing, the Slack and email alerts, and the audit log. No per-approver seats.
fields.features_subheading: Purchase orders, invoices, contracts, and expenses. Emergent builds the request form, routing, alerts, and audit database behind them.
fields.feature_1:
Request form generated with the workflow

The intake form is built with the approval workflow, not bolted on after. Every field maps to a routing rule, so the form and the process stay in sync when your policy changes.
fields.feature_2:
Sequential, parallel, or multi-level routing

One approver at a time, several in parallel, tiers by amount, or branches by department. Describe a multi-level approval rule in one sentence and it becomes the routing logic.
fields.feature_3:
Approve from Slack, Teams, or email

Every approver gets the request details and a one-click approve or reject in the channel they already use. The decision writes back to the workflow, with no separate portal.
fields.feature_4:
Escalation timers and fallback approvers

If an approver hasn't acted within your SLA, send a reminder, escalate to their manager, or hand off to a fallback approver. Set the timing in the prompt and every step follows it.
fields.feature_5:
An audit trail in a database you own

Every decision, reminder, and escalation lands in a table with requester, approver, amount, reason, and time to approve. Finance and audit query it directly, with no PDF exports.
fields.feature_6:
Full code export

The request form, the approval routing, the alerts, and the audit database all export to your GitHub. Nothing is locked inside a per-seat tool or a proprietary workflow canvas.

fields.usecase_heading: Approval Workflows You Can Build in Minutes
fields.tab_content_1:
A purchase order approval workflow that routes by amount

Tiered routing to the manager, department head, or CFO by amount, procurement added for vendors not on the approved list, a Slack alert per approver, and every decision saved with the approver chain and timestamp. Ready to connect to Xero, QuickBooks, or your ERP.
fields.tab_content_2:
An invoice approval workflow that reads the invoice for you

Invoices arrive by email or upload, an AI step extracts the vendor, amount, and line items, the workflow matches the purchase order and routes by amount and cost center, and approved invoices are written to Xero or QuickBooks with a link to the original PDF.
fields.tab_content_3:
A contract approval workflow with parallel review

Legal, finance, and the executive sponsor review in parallel, redlines go back to the counterparty, reminders fire on your SLA, and the signed copy is saved to Google Drive with every version recorded in the audit log.
fields.tab_content_4:
An expense approval workflow with a live budget check

A receipt upload form, a check against this month's spend, manager approval within policy, and finance escalation outside it. Approved expenses go to the accounting export queue; declined ones return the reason to the requester.

fields.howto_title: How to Build an Approval Workflow
fields.howto_description: Map the request, the approvers, and the rules once, and Emergent generates the request form, the routing, the alerts, and the audit log around them. Seven steps from the first request to a workflow your team actually uses.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Choose how you will build it
fields.howto_step_1_des: Approvals usually live in email chains, spreadsheets, per-seat approval tools, or workflow suites. Email and spreadsheets leave no audit trail, and per-seat tools charge for every occasional approver. Emergent generates the form, the routing, and the audit log in one build, with every approver included.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Define the trigger and the request
fields.howto_step_2_des: Name what starts the approval: a submitted form, an uploaded invoice, an inbound email, or a deal change in HubSpot. The trigger decides the request fields, such as amount, vendor, department, category, and the documents a reviewer needs to decide without asking.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write who approves what, and in what order: under $500 to the manager, $500 to $5,000 to the department head, above that to the CFO, with legal in parallel for contracts. Written as plain sentences, the matrix becomes the routing logic.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Decide what happens when an approver goes quiet: a reminder after one business day, escalation to their manager after two, and a fallback approver when someone is out of office. The SLAs you set here decide your cycle time more than any other rule.
fields.hero_prompt: Build an approval workflow for my team's purchase requests.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put approve and reject where approvers already work: Slack, Microsoft Teams, or email, with the full request context in the message. Every decision writes back to the workflow, so nobody logs in to a separate portal to clear a queue.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Decide what the audit log records
fields.howto_step_6_des: Record the requester, approver chain, amount, decision, reason, and time to approve for every request. On Emergent the log is a database table you own, so finance and audit query it directly, and a dashboard shows cycle time by approver.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Pilot with one team, then roll out
fields.howto_step_7_des: Turn it on for one team, run real requests through it for two weeks, and read time to approve from the audit log. Tighten the rules and SLAs by prompting, then roll it out to the next department, with every version kept in exportable code.
